griller.content:
# Grill: Add `slugify(title)`

> Replay: this record is scripted. It holds the recommended answers, whatever was answered in the Asks.

1. **Accented letters?** Strip the accents: `slugify('Café au lait')` is `'cafe-au-lait'`.
2. **Is an empty result an error?** No: `slugify('!!!')` returns `''`.

Also settled: a command line, `node src/cli.js <title>`, prints the slug, so the function can be tried from a shell.

spec-writer.content:
# Spec: Add `slugify(title)`

## What it does

`slugify(title)` in `src/slugify.js` turns a title into a slug for a URL or a file name:

- The slug is lowercase.
- Accents are stripped: `'Café'` becomes `'cafe'`.
- Spaces and runs of punctuation become a single dash: `slugify('Hello,  World!')` is `'hello-world'`.
- Leading and trailing dashes are trimmed: `slugify('--Hi--')` is `'hi'`.
- A title with nothing left returns `''`; it is not an error.

`node src/cli.js <title>` prints the slug of its arguments, joined by spaces.

## Testing

- `test/slugify.test.js` covers each rule above.
- `test/cli.test.js` runs the command line as a subprocess and checks what it prints.
